title: Fibre rings of a Noetherian algebra are Noetherian
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $B$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Remark Tag 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram, line 3422: B (x)_A kappa(p) = (A\p)^{-1}B/pB) with Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991: quotients and localizations of Noetherian rings are Noetherian); used without mention in more-algebra.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH1 ('on the other hand it is Noetherian')

proof.text: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the given homomorphism, $T=\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p)$, $B_{\mathfrak p}=T^{-1}B$ and $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ the ideal of $B_{\mathfrak p}$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient] there is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras (in particular of rings) $\theta:B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Remark Tag 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram, line 3422): $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS=S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S/\mathfrak pS$

proof.text: $T$ is a multiplicative subset of $B$ ($1=\varphi(1)\in T$ and $\varphi(s)\varphi(s')=\varphi(ss')$ with $ss'\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ since $\mathfrak p$ is prime), and $B\to B_{\mathfrak p}$, $b\mapsto b/1$, is the localization of $B$ at $T$. Since $B$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991): 'Any localization of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian'

proof.text: The composite $\theta^{-1}\circ\pi:B_{\mathfrak p}\to B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of the quotient map $\pi:B_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ with the inverse of the isomorphism $\theta$ of step 1 is a surjective ring homomorphism from the Noetherian ring $B_{\mathfrak p}$ (step 2). Hence $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991), proof: 'Any quotient $R/I$ of a Noetherian ring $R$ is Noetherian'
